sentences[2].whyEn: sich verlassen AUF + deren: auf deren Unterstützung.
sentences[3].whyEn: A place: wo — or in der.
sentences[7].whyEn: sprechen über: über das — or worüber.
sentences[8].whyEn: Referring to the whole clause: was.
sentences[10].whyEn: deren Antwort — possession of die Frage.
sentences[11].whyEn: After alles with a preposition: worüber.
sentences[12].whyEn: an dessen Ende — dessen stays rigid before its noun.

sentences[14].whyEn: A point in time: an dem — or als.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: That's the professor with whose support the project came about.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: We fund projects on whose results the region depends.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: die Stiftung is feminine, so the genitive relative is deren; it sits right after ohne, and Förderung follows without an article.
help.tips[0].en.text: der Autor, mit dessen Hilfe ich das Buch schrieb · die Kollegen, auf deren Unterstützung ich zähle · das Projekt, an dessen Ende … · die Frage, deren Antwort noch aussteht. The genitive relative goes right after the preposition; the noun follows without an article.
help.tips[0].en.title: Preposition + dessen / deren + noun
help.tips[0].en.trap: 'with the help of whom' becomes 'mit dessen Hilfe' — possessor first, then the thing. English order tempts 'mit der Hilfe dessen', which is wrong.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: She cancelled the conference, which disappointed many and which nobody had counted on.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The firm was in the black, which nobody had counted on.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: The clause comments on the whole sentence, and the verb is rechnen mit, so the relative is wo + mit = womit.
help.tips[1].en.text: Er hat bestanden, was alle überraschte (the fact surprised). …, womit niemand gerechnet hatte (rechnen mit). …, worauf wir gehofft hatten (hoffen auf). …, wofür ich dankbar bin. The clause comments on the whole preceding sentence.
help.tips[1].en.title: Continuing relative: , was / , womit / , worauf
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: Anyone who has been where we're going never forgets it – everything one has read about is real.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: Whoever doesn't like it can leave.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: gefallen takes the dative, so the generalising relative is wem; the main clause then picks it up with der.
help.tips[2].en.text: die Stadt, wo ich studiert habe · das Land, woher ich stamme · der Ort, wohin wir fahren · Wer das liest, (der) versteht es · Wem das nicht gefällt, der kann gehen · alles, worüber wir sprachen · das, wovon ich träume.
help.tips[2].en.title: wo / wohin / woher; wer … der; alles, worüber
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: That is the best thing I have ever read.
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: alles is a pronoun, not a noun, so the relative is was.
help.tips[3].en.text: A noun → der/die/das (with dessen/deren for possession). A place → wo/wohin/woher. A pronoun / superlative / whole clause → was, or wo(r)- + preposition. A general person → wer.
help.tips[3].en.title: Which relative? Ask what it refers to
help.context.en: The colleague with whose help I completed the evaluation comes from the city where I studied. Anyone who knows her knows: everything she takes on gets done thoroughly – which the team appreciates and which the management now firmly counts on. The project, at the end of which stands a joint book, takes us back to where we both come from.
help.mistakes[1].whyEn: A whole clause is referred to with was.
help.hookEn: mit deren Hilfe, womit niemand rechnete, alles, worüber wir sprachen: master these joints and long German sentences stop falling apart.
help.introEn: Relative clauses in formal German use every corner of the system. Genitive with a preposition: der Autor, mit dessen Hilfe …; die Kollegen, auf deren Unterstützung …; die Firma, deren Produkte … — dessen / deren sit directly after the preposition and before the noun, no article. Place words: wo / wohin / woher for places and, in speech, for times (der Tag, wo …). Generalising: wer … (der), wen … (den), wem … (dem). Preposition + pronoun for nouns (das Thema, über das …) and wo(r)- for things and pronouns (alles, worüber …; das, wovon …). The continuing relative clause (weiterführender Nebensatz) that comments on a whole sentence: Er hat bestanden, was alle überraschte; …, womit niemand gerechnet hatte; …, worauf wir gehofft hatten — was for a subject/object, wo(r)- + preposition when the verb needs one (rechnen mit → womit; hoffen auf → worauf). These are the joints of long written sentences, and following an article or a report depends on tracking them. The gaps are the relative words themselves — with their preposition where the verb or noun demands one — so every item asks which form the antecedent and the verb require.
help.rememberEn[0]: mit dessen Hilfe, auf deren Unterstützung: preposition + genitive relative + bare noun.
help.rememberEn[1]: , was (fact) / , womit, worauf (verb + preposition): the commenting clause.
help.recallEn.known: From the relative-clause lessons: der, dessen, denen, wer and was.
help.recallEn.today: Relatives that point at a whole clause (womit, worüber) and mit deren Hilfe.
